title: Brand-inversion-safe button & table grid adaptor for dense console states
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As we extend brand theming across customer consoles, a recurring issue appears when a partner brand uses an accent that inverts semantics under dark mode (strong brand color used both as accent and as surface). Current token fallbacks make table rows, compact controls, and primary buttons either low-contrast or visually noisy when the brand accent flips in dark.

Goal: Deliver a token mapping and component override adaptor that ensures: (1) primary/secondary buttons retain WCAG AA+ contrast in both light and dark with brand-accent-driven themes, (2) dense table/grid states (row hover/selected/focused) preserve row legibility and separators, and (3) small interactive controls (pill filters, compact menus) avoid color collisions with chart strokes and data badges. Implementation must be compatible with the Console theme engine and support a feature-flagged rollout per-customer.

Scope: Design token mapping logic for brand-inversion cases; component-level overrides for Button, TableRow, DataGrid, Badge, and CompactPills; visual examples for 4 brand accent luminance buckets; accessibility rules; handoff assets for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Primary buttons with any brand accent must have contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 on their computed background in both light and dark modes when shown at normal and disabled states.
2) Table row hover/selected/focused states remain distinguishable at 10px row height and with zebra disabled.
3) Compact controls (<=28px height) do not reuse the exact brand-accent fill when that would reduce chart/legend contrast.
4) Token adaptor is behind a per-tenant flag; console shows a rollback toggle and falls back to existing token mapping when disabled.
5) Visual diff snapshots for 6 example brands pass automated regression checks (no more than 3% pixel diff in allowed regions).
design_notes:
High-level adaptor behavior: when theme.brand_inversion_behavior == 'smart-invert' then compute: 
- brand-accent-foreground = tone(brand-accent, 'on-accent-contrast') which maps to either white or neutral-900 depending on luminance threshold.
- brand-accent-surface = blend(brand-accent, neutral-surface, 12%) for backgrounds used behind pills/badges in dark mode.
- button-primary-bg maps to brand-accent when brand-accent-contrast >= 4.5 otherwise to brand-accent-elevated (brand-accent desaturated by 18%).
- table-row-selected-bg uses neutral-elevation-2 + 6% brand-accent overlay (preserves row text contrast).
- separator color remains semantic-separator even when accent saturations are high to avoid collision.

Examples (illustrative):
- Brand A (vivid cobalt, L=18): in dark -> primary button uses brand-accent-elevated + on-accent white; selected-row overlays use neutral-elevation-2.
- Brand B (muted lime, L=62): in light -> primary button uses brand-accent directly; in dark -> primary button falls back to neutral-100 with 14% brand tint to keep contrast.

Design tokens to add: brand-accent-elevated, brand-accent-overlay-6, brand-accent-on-contrast, table-selected-overlay, compact-control-surface. Add metadata flags: "inversion-safe" and "brand-intent" to guide runtime selection.
implementation_tasks: Create token spec and add new tokens to token-json (brand-accent-elevated, brand-accent-overlay-6, brand-accent-on-contrast, table-selected-overlay, compact-control-surface)
Update Button component to accept theme.hint.brand_inversion and compute bg/fg via token adaptor; add unit tests for focus/hover/disabled states
Update Table and DataGrid components: row hover/selected/focus states to use table-selected-overlay and maintain separator tone
Add feature flag (console feature-flag service) per-tenant: 'brand-inversion-adaptor' with server-side toggle
Create automated visual tests (Percy) for 6 curated brands across light/dark and dense/compact densities
Engineering pairing session: handoff runbook + Figma walkthrough (design + eng sync)
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Trade-off: Strong desaturation helps contrast but reduces perceived brand fidelity. We document that brand fidelity may be intentionally reduced under dark mode for accessibility.
- Risk: Backwards incompatible tokens could impact third-party brand overrides; mitigation: versioned token release and per-tenant feature flag.
- Performance risk: runtime token computation per-request could add overhead; mitigation: compute and cache derived tokens at theme load instead of per-render.
- Edge case: customer-managed CSS overrides may override adaptor; include guidance and a detection heuristic to log overrides during rollout.
qa_checklist: Run visual snapshot suite for each brand in list: Brand A, Brand B, Brand C, Brand D, Brand E, Brand F
Contrast audit using axe-core for buttons, table rows, and compact controls across states
Manual exploratory pass on Legacy Console and New Console density modes
Feature-flag toggle test: enable/disable per-tenant and verify UI reverts cleanly
Accessibility keyboard-only navigation test for focused row and button states
